claims.text: The local row, Bulbapedia, PokeBoon, and Pokumon place the How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 2 Psyduck insert route in September 1999, with Bulbapedia giving the first-edition publication date as September 22, 1999.
Bulbapedia identifies volume 2 as the second of six How I Became a Pokemon Card manga volumes and states that its included promo card is Psyduck.
Bulbapedia lists the first edition as a Japanese Kadokawa-Media Factory publication with ISBN 4889917284.

Bulbapedia lists volume 2 chapters PW08 through PW14, including 'Troubled Pokemon, Psyduck', so the promo belongs to a book whose contents directly frame Psyduck as a story subject rather than just a pack pull.

Bulbapedia identifies How I Became a Pokemon Card as created by 姫野かげまる / Kagemaru Himeno and says each book promo and the cards featured in the chapters were originally illustrated by Himeno; Bulbapedia's Psyduck page credits the Natta Wake / Wizards Promo artwork to Kagemaru Himeno.

Bulbapedia's Himeno profile describes her early Pokemon work, watercolor and bright soft-tone style, long-running TCG contribution, and own How I Became a Pokemon Card series, making this promo both a card and a creator-authored explanation of card art.

Bulbapedia describes the manga's premise as stories that expand on actual Pokemon card images and tell what the Pokemon is doing or how it got there; this makes Natta Wake Psyduck unusually meta, because the source object is a book explaining its own promo image.

Bulbapedia says the Japanese Unnumbered Promotional Psyduck print was included with How I Became a Pokemon Card volume 2, has a color graphic of an open book with a trading card in place of an expansion symbol, and has bottom-border text reading 'Pokemon Card Books "How I Became a Pokemon Card" bonus card.'

Bulbapedia places the same card page across Fossil / Mystery of the Fossils, Pokemon TCG GB appearances, Wizards Black Star Promo 20, and the Japanese Unnumbered Promotional Natta Wake print; agents should preserve that lineage while not collapsing those releases into one physical object.

Agents should keep this Vol. 2 book route separate from Fossil 53 / Mystery of the Fossils Psyduck, Wizards Black Star Promo 20 '? Psyduck', Pokemon TCG GB sprites, later Psyduck cards, generic How I Became a Pokemon Card lots, and book-only listings without card evidence.

The legible target is Psyduck plus How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 2 route plus open-book symbol / bottom-border bonus-card evidence; catalog facts do not prove possession, authenticity, condition, price, complete book state, sealed book state, or spendability.

steps: Record the seller's exact route language: How I Became a Pokemon Card, Pokemon Card ni Natta Wake, Vol. 2, Psyduck, Koduck, コダック, book insert, or generic Fossil/Wizards promo.
Confirm the offered card is Psyduck / コダック and not Fossil 53, Mystery of the Fossils, Wizards Black Star Promo 20 '? Psyduck', a TCG GB sprite reference, or a later Psyduck card.
Ask for seller-controlled front and back images before using catalog or community images as more than reference comparison.
Inspect the expansion-symbol area for the color open-book-with-trading-card graphic; do not treat a Fossil symbol, Wizards star number, or unreadable symbol area as a pass.
Inspect the bottom border for the Pokemon Card Books 'How I Became a Pokemon Card' bonus-card sentence.

If book provenance is claimed, request book cover, volume number, ISBN/copyright page, insert pocket, bag/obi, or purchase-bundle evidence separately; the card alone does not prove complete book state.

Keep price, grade, authenticity, condition, official copy count, sealed book status, complete book packaging, and spendability outside catalog authority until seller-controlled evidence and any verifier process are present.

narrative.human_title: How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 2: Psyduck gets explained
narrative.why_it_matters: Vol. 2 is a beautiful proof of why this catalog should care about assembly. Psyduck is already a creature of visible confusion, and Natta Wake turns that confusion into a premise: the manga does not merely include a promo, it tells you why the picture exists. The book, the card, Himeno's hand, and the open-book symbol are one little machine for making card art feel inhabited.

card_highlights.why_it_matters: Psyduck matters here because the Natta Wake route gives a nervous, headache-prone Pokemon a book-world explanation. The attacks are Headache and Fury Swipes; the manga chapter is Troubled Pokemon, Psyduck; the card becomes more than a Water common lineage because its confusion is made narratively useful.

claims.text: The local catalog and Bulbapedia identify source index 131 as Psyduck, Japanese コダック / Koduck.
Bulbapedia says the Japanese Unnumbered Promotional Psyduck print was included with How I Became a Pokemon Card volume 2, released on September 22, 1999.
Bulbapedia credits the Natta Wake / Wizards Promo artwork to 姫野かげまる / Kagemaru Himeno.
Bulbapedia transcribes Psyduck's attacks as Headache and Fury Swipes and identifies it as a Water Basic Pokemon; the manga volume includes a chapter called 'Troubled Pokemon, Psyduck'.

Bulbapedia says the Japanese Unnumbered Promotional print has a color graphic of an open book with a trading card in place of an expansion symbol and bottom-border text naming it as a Pokemon Card Books How I Became a Pokemon Card bonus card.

Bulbapedia says the Wizards Black Star Promo 20 print is commonly known as '? Psyduck' and the Japanese Unnumbered Promotional print is similarly known as Natta Wake Psyduck, making nickname-based matching useful but not sufficient.

Bulbapedia's Kagemaru Himeno profile describes her Pokemon work since the early TCG years, including Pokemon Tales and the How I Became a Pokemon Card series, plus a recognizable watercolor style with soft bright tones.

This Psyduck is a strong catalog object because the Pokemon's headache/confusion theme, the volume's Troubled Pokemon chapter, and Himeno's story-frame all point in the same direction: the card image has a narrative reason to exist.
Agents should not match by Psyduck, Kagemaru Himeno, or '? Psyduck' nickname alone; the row requires the How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 2 route and the open-book / bonus-card print evidence.

The catalog can make the route and visible-tell checklist legible, but it does not prove the seller owns the card, that a shown card is authentic, that the book is complete or sealed, that condition is true, that price is fair, or that the row is spendable.

narrative.human_title: Psyduck 131: the headache gets a story
narrative.why_it_matters: This Psyduck has the best kind of silliness: it is funny because it is specific. Headache, troubled Pokemon, vacant look, mysterious powers, Himeno's soft storybook eye, and the Natta Wake premise all gather around one small promo. The catalog should preserve that warmth while still forcing the hard checks: open-book symbol, bonus-card footer, Vol. 2 route.
